title: Jim Thorpe Weekend/Bike Train
description:
Lancaster Bicycle Club (LBC) Meetup
Join members and friends for a weekend of bicycle riding in Jim Thorpe.
Check into the hotel on Friday, November 13th.
On Saturday check in at train station at 8am for the 9:15 am train to White Haven.
**Lehigh Gorge Scenic Railway Bike Train Rail Trail Ride:**
1 Susquehanna Street, Jim Thorpe, PA.
They start to load bikes at 8:00am; train departs promptly at 9:15am. Bring a packed lunch.
We will plan to stop for lunch along the trail at one of the picnic spots. We will ride the historic train up through the Gorge with our bikes, about one hour, to White Haven. Then we will ride the crushed stone rail trail back along the Scenic Lehigh Gorge to Jim Thorpe. You must purchase your train ticket in advance, $39. Call 570-325-8485 to purchase your ticket , visit [www.lgsry.com](http://www.lgsry.com) for more information. Please note that there are no refunds on tickets if the ride is cancelled or if, due to inclement weather, the train does not run that day. However, bike train tickets do not expire and can be used another day. There is no free parking in Jim Thorpe, $10/day (cash only)per vehicle to park in municipal lot, where the train station is located, at 1 Susquehanna Street, Jim Thorpe, PA.
Your $39 ticket is for those who are bringing your own bike. These tickets are limited. It cost double to rent one of their bikes. You must make your decision and buy a ticket two months in advance. Helmets are mandatory for all of our rides. Parking lot has an attendant and is patrolled.
3 minute video of bike train and rail trail:
[https://youtu.be/2KYaJWwh9D0](https://youtu.be/2KYaJWwh9D0)
On Sunday morning we will check out of the hotel and at 9am we will meet in Jim Thorpe at the trailhead , Packer Hill Road, for the Switchback trail, biking 9 miles to Summit Hill and back. This is a gravel trail. Afterwards… those who want to go out to lunch together before traveling home.

title: Make & Take: Sourdough Bread for Beginners
location: Bird-in-Hand Artisan Village, 2705 Old Philadelphia Pike, Bird-in-Hand, PA, 17505, United States
description:
Join us if you love to bake! 
In recent years, it seems everybody’s been talking about sourdough. Still, this delicious bread is a bit of a mystery to many. If you’re curious about sourdough, join us for this hour-long class. Amelia Detwiler of Willow House Goods will talk about how sourdough is different from other types of breads, and she’ll demonstrate the care and feeding of sourdough starter and discuss the basics of the first bake. 
Each guest will go home with a Sourdough Starter Kit that includes everything they need to start baking immediately: 

1 jar of active, hydrated, ready-to use sourdough starter
A professional-grade class fermentation jar that they can use to hold and maintain their starter
A traditional wooden spurtle to stir deep into the jar for a perfect mix with less mess
A stylish breathable cotton bonnet for the jar
Professional instruction sheets, including step-by-step feeding guides and schedule, a beginner-friendly recipe, and trouble-shooting tips

Sourdough has prebiotics, or healthy gut bacteria. It also has less gluten and a lower glycemic index than some other breads. 
Two sessions are available, starting at 10 a.m. or 1 p.m. Walk-ins are welcome if space is available, but reservations are strongly recommended. 
$65 per person includes instruction and Sourdough Starter Kit. 
Date: Saturday, November 14 
Times: 10 a.m. and 1 p.m. 
To save your space: Call (717) 344-6875. Reservations strongly recommended.

title: Lancaster Breakfast and History Walking Tour
location: Unique Lancaster, 23 N Walnut Street, Lancaster, 17603, United States
description:
Searching for a walking history tour in Lancaster? You’re in for a flavorful experience—literally! 


Introducing the Lancaster History & Breakfast Walking Tour—a dynamic two-hour adventure that blends the rich heritage of one of America’s oldest inland cities with a delicious morning meal. Explore Lancaster’s vibrant streets with a professionally trained local guide and journey through time from the early 1700s through the transformative decades of the 20th century. 


Brought to you by Unique Lancaster Experiences, this guided walk kicks off with your choice of hot or iced coffee or tea to energize your morning. Along the way, you’ll hear engaging stories about Lancaster’s evolution as a bustling Market City and its transition from trolleys to automobiles after WWI. 


But this isn’t your standard history tour. You’ll dive into interactive discussions and uncover captivating insights about colonial life, architectural landmarks, and the impact of prohibition on the region. 


As you explore, you’ll stop at five handpicked local spots to enjoy a curated tasting menu featuring hearty breakfast sandwiches, fresh fruits, sweet pastries, and other morning favorites. 


Please note: This tour offers vegetarian-friendly options only. If you have other dietary needs, we recommend our International Food Tour for a better fit. 


Whether you’re passionate about history, love discovering new flavors, or just want a memorable way to see the city, the Lancaster History & Breakfast Tour is a great choice for solo explorers, couples, and groups alike.

title: Wonder Zone Grand Opening Weekend!
location: The Lancaster Science Factory, 454 New Holland Ave, Lancaster, PA, 17602, United States
description:
Join Lancaster Science Factory to celebrate the Grand Opening Weekend of the Wonder Zone! The Wonder Zone is a brand new exhibit area designed for kids ages 3-5, but accessible and enjoyable for all ages! This exhibit are was made possible by a generous lead donation from the Dart Foundation. Thank you! 
Wonder Zone Weekend Timeline:
Saturday, November 14th 
9:00am-10:00am        Members ONLY Morning. 

Lancaster Science Factory members are invited to experience the Wonder Zone early! Please RSVP to this event through the linked Eventbrite. This event is free for members, just be sure to bring your membership card!

10:00am-1:00pm       Lancaster Libraries, Intermediate Unit 13, and Lancaster Rec Activities 

 Join us to explore the Wonder Zone! To help us celebrate, our friends from Lancaster Libraries will have the Bookmobile on site and do hourly story times in the Castagna Learning Center. 
Lancaster Rec and Intermediate Unit 13 will have hands-on STEM and literacy-based activities on the exhibit floor.   

Sunday, November 15th 
1:00 and 3:00             Starry Night Slime Lab 

Continue the Wonder Zone celebrations on Sunday with Starry Night Slime Lab! Join us for a 30-minute guided hands-on workshop where participants will create their own slime. Learn how a few simple ingredients come together to make this stretchy- squishy favorite! Workshops will take place twice each scheduled day, so choose the time that works best for you!
This slime lab is specially themed to match our new Reach exhibit and donor wall in the Wonder Zone, so be sure to check it out while you are here!

About the Wonder Zone:
Join us for the grand opening of the Wonder Zone, 12 exhibit experiences themed around light, sound, forces and motion, and engineering. This space was designed to be accessible to kids ages 3-5 years old and their families, but will be enjoyed by all.

Some of the new exhibit experiences include:

Everbright, an  interactive light wall made of hundreds of dials that change colors when you turn them. Think the Lite-Brite of your childhood, but with hundreds of analog dials and no removable parts.
Ramps and Magneticars- (see the example) – design your car using the large, foam magnetic pieces. Design your ramp. Can you make an ice cream truck that goes slow? A race car that goes fast?
Immersive air exhibit – Step inside the circle and float balls or scarves on a stream of air that you can interact with.
Shape projector – explore light, color and shadow with the shape projector!

description:
The Creative House of Lancaster
#### ***A Place to Make Art Together***

**When:** Every Other Saturday from 10am - 12pm
**Where:** [The Candy Factory](https://share.google/nqC7VtCS6IcDeBRyg)
**Cost:** Free & Open to the Public
**Ages:** All Ages

**Upcoming Dates**
July 11, July 25, Aug 8, Aug 22, Sept 5, Sept 19, Oct 3, Oct 17, Oct 31, Nov 14, Nov 28, Dec 9, Dec 23

*Do you have creative aspirations but never seem to make the time? Do you want the companionship of others to overcome your creative blocks and “just do it”?*

Creative Release provides spaces and resources that make artmaking accessible. Whether you’re an experienced artist or just looking to explore your creative side, Creative Release is a safe place to explore your ideas with others. Bring your ongoing projects or use the art materials available.

Don't have a project at the moment? That's just fine. I’ll have materials to share.

* A welcoming, inclusive environment
* A variety of art materials to experiment with
* Demonstrations on how to use different art materials
* The opportunity to work on your personal projects
* The chance to meet and collaborate with fellow creatives
* A moment to relax, create, and escape the usual routine

Anyone and everyone! Bring an idea for a card, a knitting pattern you’ve been wanting to try, a shirt that needs mending, or a full-on canvas and paints. Most of all, bring your lovely self! We believe in the power of community and creativity.

title: LFS Feminist Consciousness-Raising Film Afternoons
description:
Lancaster Freethought Society
**Feminist Film Afternoons #1: Made in Dagenham (2010)**
**What happens when women stop cooperating with a system that depends on their labor but refuses to value it?**
Join us for the first of five Feminist Consciousness-Raising Film Afternoons, featuring *Made in Dagenham*, the spirited, funny, and inspiring true story of women workers at Ford's Dagenham factory in England.
In 1968, women sewing machinists discover that their work has been classified as unskilled and paid less than men's. Rather than accept it, they organize, strike, and help launch a movement for equal pay.

**After the film, we'll discuss:**

* What changed when these women recognized their shared situation?
* Why was withdrawing their labor more effective than simply demanding fair treatment?
* What could women accomplish today by collectively withdrawing their cooperation from unequal systems?

This is a relaxed, friendly afternoon of film and conversation—not a lecture or debate. Everyone is welcome to bring their own experiences and perspectives.

**The Details**

* **When:** Sunday, November 15, 2–5 PM
* **Where:** My home in Millersville. Address provided privately to confirmed attendees.
* **Seating:** Limited to six guests.
* **Attendance:** Women have priority through Saturday. If spaces remain, men may RSVP beginning Saturday, November 14 at noon. Please respect this reservation arrangement.
* **Guests:** No additional guests, please.

This is the first of five independent film afternoons, held every other Sunday through January 10. Come to one or come to several—there's no commitment to attend the entire series.
**Bring your curiosity, your ideas, and your willingness to imagine something better!**

title: Marching to Independence: Lancaster Soldiers at the Battle of Fort Lee
location: Manheim Township, MTP Morgan Center B
description:
Community, Presentation, Adults, Seniors

How did ordinary men from Lancaster County end up on the front lines of the American Revolution? Step back in time with living historian Samuel Leamer to uncover the harrowing story of Clotz's Battalion-- part of the legendary "Flying Camp" mobile reserve.Relive the tension of November 1776 at the Battle of Fort Lee, discover the courageous stories of local soldiers fighting for a brand-new nation, and see how modern historians uncover the past to keep their legacy alive. Don't miss this immersive journey into the fight for independence!Registration is encouraged!A Berks County native and Cairn University history graduate, Presenter Sam Leamer has spent a lifetime bringing the past to life through reenactments-- and a decade mastering the art of modern coffee. By blending historical scholarship with coffee expertise, Sam offers a richer, deeper look into Colonial Coffee Culture, showing how the humble coffee bean helped fuel America’s fight for independence.

The short service of Compline is based on the closing time of prayer in the Daily Office, or monastic cycle of prayer. It is observed in monasteries around 8 or 9 PM when darkness has fallen and bedtime is near. 

The thoughts that inspire the prayers during Compline are the need for divine forgiveness and protection against the powers of darkness. Prayers for peace and rest are offered as night falls. 

People of all faiths and beliefs are invited to this contemplative service. The service lasts about 20 minutes.

No experience in any system is required and anyone interested in dipping their toes into the TTRPG world are welcomed and encouraged to join in on the fun! This month's game is Mothership!An Anti-Corporate Suicide RunThe stars were a dream for us all - unlimited freedom in every direction imaginable. What we got instead was a corporate hellscape expanding exponentially, forever.Now it comes for the Dream. Prospero’s Dream is a space station of enormous scale. Once owned by corporate interests and now ferociously independent, it is not a nice place to live, but those that live there are free from the corporate yoke. At least they were.First welcomed as a partner in stability and profit within Prospero’s Dream, METAStatic, Inc. has spread and festered, bloating within every crack it can find in the station. They promised to stabilize the station’s O2 shortage. Instead, they found an unlimited labor source in The Choke, taking debtors on their last legs and turning them into debt slaves. The station is being flooded with pro-corporate propaganda and the presence of MSI’s private military force, the Peacemakers, is an ever more common sight. Execs walk around in premium sleeves while people beg for a handful of credits to fill their O2 credsticks.All that power, all that entitlement, all focused in a single corporate megabuilding at the heart of the dream. You are the lit match and this tower is the tinder. Burn it all down. Give the Dream a fresh start.Even if you're not there to see it. Registration is required. This group is for adults only.

title: Tellus AfterDark: Cuffing Season
location: Tellus360, 24 East King Street, Lancaster, Pennsylvania, 17603, United States
description:
The nights are getting colder, and nobody wants to spend another winter swiping. Tellus AfterDark is back. Here’s the deal: A host checks you in and hands you a name tag. You start at small tables with a game that does the flirting-opener for you, so nobody has to break the ice alone. Then the room opens up and it’s on you. Grab a drink on your own tab, find the person you were eyeing across the table, and see where it goes. Come solo or bring your wingwoman. Everyone in the room came out for the same reason you did. 21+. Your winter plans start here. How the night works. You check in with a host and get a name tag — there’s nothing to download and no profile to fill out at the door. The evening runs in three movements. First, you’re seated at a small table with a game to play — that’s the icebreaker, so nobody has to invent an opening line cold — and the men move one table along each round, which means every round is a genuinely new set of people. Then the structure drops away and it’s open mingling: go where you want, talk to whoever you want, for as long as it’s working. By that point you’ve already met most of the room, so nobody is starting cold — which is the part a bar full of strangers never gets right. Last, one-on-ones with the people you haven’t already sat with. Near the end you privately note anyone you’d like to see again, and nobody else sees it. If someone noted you back, that’s a match, and you both get it that night rather than after some review period. Why it’s built this way. Everyone in the room came out on purpose on a Wednesday night. That’s a filter no dating app has. The structure does the hard part — you never have to work out how to start or end a conversation — and the other awkward part, finding out whether it was mutual, is handled quietly for you afterwards.

Click here to join Compline. (This link can be used for every evening Compline on Zoom.) 

The short service of Compline is based on the closing time of prayer in the Daily Office, or monastic cycle of prayer. It is observed in monasteries around 8 or 9 PM when darkness has fallen and bedtime is near. 

The thoughts that inspire the prayers during Compline are the need for divine forgiveness and protection against the powers of darkness. Prayers for peace and rest are offered as night falls. 

People of all faiths and beliefs are invited to this contemplative service. The service lasts about 20 minutes.

location: LancasterHistory Museum & Research Center, 230 N. President Avenue, 230 N. President Avenue, PA, 17603, United States
description:
One built an empire with a Kiss and the other designed it. This is the untold story of Milton S. Hershey and his architect, C. Emlen Urban. What drove these two men to achieve goals and fame beyond their wildest dreams? Why is one an American icon and the other unknown beyond his hometown? Drawn from his new book, Urban and the Chocolate King, architect and historian Gregg Scott joins LancasterHistory to tell the tale of two men who met as young boys in the small town of Lancaster, PA, and began a journey of design and construction that endured for fifty years.  



Gregg Scott is a Fellow of the American Institute of Architects, a partner emeritus and co-founder of RLPS Architects, a monthly columnist for LNP, and twice recipient of the Journalist and Educators Award presented by the Historic Preservation Trust of Lancaster County. Most recently, the author of Urban Legend, Urban Alphabet, and the 2026 fall release of Urban and the Chocolate King.

title: Lincoln and the Founders: Completing the Unfinished Work
location: Columbia, COL Meeting Room
description:
Community, Presentation, Teens, Adults, Seniors, Everyone

In the Gettysburg Address, Abraham Lincoln said that the nation should be dedicated "to the unfinished work which they who fought here have thus far so nobly advanced." What was this unfinished work? When Lincoln started his famous address with "Four score and seven years ago," he hearkened back to the year 1776 and the Declaration of Independence that stated that "all men are created equal."Much of Lincoln's political ideology stemmed from the Declaration of Independence. His words and policies before and during the Civil War demonstrate his reverence for the Declaration. While Lincoln was not an abolitionist, he did believe that slavery should be put in "the course of ultimate extinction" by preventing its spread to the territories.As President, Lincoln originally worked to preserve the Union that the Founders created. As the Civil War progressed, he realized that he could no longer restore the Union as it was. He had to restore the Union so that it was worth saving and to prevent further division over this issue in the future.This program discusses how Lincoln's ideas and policies constantly evolved throughout his political career up to the passage of the 13th Amendment which Lincoln declared "a King's curse" for the issue of slavery in America.

description:
Our November America 250 selection, Lee Isaac Chung’s Minari, follows a Korean American family pursuing a new life on a small Arkansas farm in the early 1980s.

It is a deeply American story of immigration, land, work, faith, family, and reinvention—but also a searching examination of the costs hidden within the American dream. Who bears the burden of one person’s ambition? Does independence ever exist without care and dependency? What transforms a piece of land into a home?

Arriving during harvest and Thanksgiving season, Minari also asks us to think about cultivation and gratitude: whose labor sustains a family, whose histories inhabit the land, and what conditions allow transplanted lives to flourish. Its answer is both modest and profound: nothing grows entirely on its own.

title: Using Grok Bot to Recover Websites While I Sleep + 2026 Year-End Review
description:
WordPress Lancaster
This month, **Austin Ginder** will show how he uses **Grok Bot**, a team of AI routines, to watch and repair WordPress sites overnight. Every 30 minutes, a down-site watcher checks for outages, connects over SSH and works out what broke. When the cause is bad code, it fixes it and writes up what it changed. In its first nine days it patched about a dozen live sites, mostly while Austin was asleep.

**What we'll cover:**

* How the watcher sorts an outage: fixable, not ours, or hands off
* The fix order: update, roll back, patch, and deactivate only as a last resort
* Real fixes from the past month, including PHP 8 fatals, a Gravity Forms class change and a disabled PHP function
* The steps after every fix: back up, purge cache, confirm the site loads, and log the change
* Reviewing security signals the same way: an overnight run covered 226 findings across 206 sites
* The guardrails, what it still gets wrong, and why it runs on Austin's Mac for now

After the talk we'll do a **year-end review**. We'll look back at what we covered in 2026, share what changed in our own WordPress work this year, and collect ideas for topics and speakers for 2027.

This is our last meetup of the year. We're skipping December and will be back on the regular schedule (third Thursday) on **January 21, 2027**.

Pizza 🍕 and introductions at 7pm.

Click here to join Compline. (This link can be used for every evening Compline on Zoom.) 

The short service of Compline is based on the closing time of prayer in the Daily Office, or monastic cycle of prayer. It is observed in monasteries around 8 or 9 PM when darkness has fallen and bedtime is near. 

The thoughts that inspire the prayers during Compline are the need for divine forgiveness and protection against the powers of darkness. Prayers for peace and rest are offered as night falls. 

People of all faiths and beliefs are invited to this contemplative service. The service lasts about 20 minutes.

title: Ride the Pa Abandoned Turnpike 20 F
description:
Lancaster Bicycle Club (LBC) Meetup
Join members and friends of the Lancaster Bicycle Club and Rails for Trails for a bike ride through the abandoned tunnels of the Pennsylvania Turnpike. When the turnpike was expanded to go over the mountain at Breezewood, three tunnels and a plaza were abandoned. The trail is 10 miles long and flat.

From Lancaster
We will meet together, leaving the parking lot of Walmart, the 222 Ephrata exit on Saturday morning, November 21st at 8am. Use Meet Up comments to make arrangements and please carpool. We will drive North one exit on 222, getting on the Turnpike and driving West to the Breezwood exit. This is a 1 and ½ hour drive. After getting off the turnpike we will meet re-group at the exit at Scheetz.
From Maryland
Drive directly to the in intersection of Rt. 30 and the Pa Turnpike exit at Breezwood. Everyone meeting at Sheetz at 10am.
The entrance to the trail is 1/2 mile away, route 30 and Tannery Road.

Caution
-since 1968 the trail has been abandoned. It is mostly gravel now.
-no road bikes…
-there are no lights in these tunnels. You must have bright front lights on you bicycles.
-one tunnel is 1 ½ mile long, completely dark.
After returning to Breezwood, we will hang out and eat together at Bob Evan’s. Each rider will wear a helmet and have a tube for you or someone to fix.
Richard Conner, leader

title: Layer the Walls: Turn of the Century
location: Ware Center for the Arts, 42 N. Prince St., Lancaster, PA, 17603, United States
description:
In one Lower East Side tenement, forty layers of wallpaper were found clinging to the walls—each piece applied by a new immigrant family. Using puppetry, masks, and live action, Layer the Walls tells the incredible stories held within each layer—an Irish immigrant helping to build the Brooklyn Bridge, Italian brothers surviving the Great Blizzard of 1888, and two Russian Jewish garment workers joining the Uprising of 20,000 to fight for safety. Recommended for ages 8 and up. 

2 pm • Free kids’ activities and crafts in the lobby!

title: Klezmer and Jewish Music by members of Quartet Harriet: Christopher Brooks, violin and Laurie Reese, violoncello
location: Lititz, LTZ Community Room
description:
Music, Everyone

Join us for an evening of Klezmer and Jewish music. Klezmer music is traditional instrumental music of the Ashkenazi Jews. Meet the musicians; Christopher Brooks was born and raised in Brooklyn, New York. He began studying the violin at PS 8 in Brooklyn Heights and at the Third Street Music School. Attending the New School of Music in Philadelphia, Mr. Brooks studied violin with Jascha Brodsky and Geoffrey Michaels. He has played chamber music and been a member of numerous orchestras. Laurie Haines Reese is a cellist dedicated to creating and performing music—especially new music—that explores the cello’s creative possibilities. An accomplished classical musician with a lifelong curiosity about what else the cello can do, she is equally at home in folk, jazz, improvisatory, and experimental music. Based in Lancaster, PA, Laurie has freelanced and concertized extensively throughout the United States and Europe.This performance is made possible through a grant from the Yiddish Book Center. Yiddish Book Center

location: Quarryville, QVL Story Corner/Early Literacy Lab

Medicare Annual Open Enrollment Appointments at Quarryville LibraryLancaster County Office of Aging runs a program called PA Medi, formerly APPRISE. This group assists those with questions about Medicare, Medicaid, and other health insurance all year round.   They will be scheduling appointments in their office: 150 N. Queen St., Lancaster, and at other sites all over the county during October – December, 2026.  Please call 717-299-7979 to set up an appointment at Quarryville Library or elsewhere. They will meet with you individually, confidentially, to go over what Medicare Plan you currently have, and to see if upcoming 2027 plans are the same, have higher premiums, are still available, etc.  If your coverage remains the same and you like it, you don’t have to do anything.  Drug or RX plans are those you can switch at this time of year. You can also switch from an Advantage Plan to another Advantage Plan or to an Original Medicare Plan. Insurance changes made during the Open Enrollment time become effective January 1, 2027.

Shakedown Citi is a fresh new force on the jam band scene, born in the heart of a Grateful Dead parking lot at Citi Field in 2023.  When the band’s members crossed paths on Shakedown Street, something clicked – and the music hasn’t stopped since. 
Rather than imitating the Dead, Shakedown Citi channels their spirit – creating spontaneous, soulful performances that feel alive, adventurous and totally in the moment. Each set is a journey, full of unexpected twists, deep grooves and musical conversation that pulls even the most skeptical listener into the vibe.  Every Shakedown Citi show begins long before the first note.  Each setlist is thoughtfully and meticulously crafted from the Dead repertoire, affiliated catalogs and beyond, balancing deep cuts and beloved anthems, rarities and reprises.  No two nights are ever the same – each performance stands as a work of art on its own, alive in its moment, while also fitting into the larger patchwork of the repertoire.   
It’s not just a tribute – it’s the Dead, reborn.

Presented by Big Fan Presents
—————————————————
The Small Town Titans return to Mickey’s Black Box for their annual Home Town Holiday Show! 
The Small Town Titans are an American rock n’ roll power trio from York, PA who love to constantly create, as well as play live. Gone is the notion that a rock band should only release 10 songs at a time every 2 years. In a world where music fans crave new content constantly, the Small Town Titans aim to deliver their brand of art all of the time, drawing inspiration from a newer wave of rock bands such as Highly Suspect and Royal Blood, and rock legends such as the Foo Fighters, Audioslave, and Deep Purple. Thanks to their efforts at taking matters into their own hands, STT can create and release songs, podcasts, live online concerts, and more with no rules. In a social media driven world, STT knows releasing quality, constant content is as important as playing great live shows. 
In November of 2018, the band’s cover of the Christmas song “You’re a Mean One, Mr. Grinch” went viral in a matter of days, leading to charting on various Billboard charts including Holiday Digital Song Sales, Rock Digital Song Sales, Emerging Artists, and reaching #5 on the Next Big Sound chart. The song also reached #2 on the iTunes Rock charts, only being surpassed by Queen’s “Bohemian Rhapsody”. STT quickly found themselves achieving success, all on their own terms. As a continued unsigned act, all three members have risen to the occasion to continue to make music the way they want to, free from having to follow traditional music industry rules. By changing their mindset and focus towards creating content like many successful YouTubers, STT has made fans the old fashioned way, by word of mouth. 
With no manager, label, or radio support, the Small Town Titans have managed to find success by simply never forgetting one thing, their fans, both new and old. Instead of trying to make a million fans, STT is focusing on the fans they already have, and the ones they continue to make. With a love for playing live, a Small Town Titans show has evolved into more than a concert. It’s an event, with a set list that’s decided right before the show, and plenty of stage banter in between songs. The band simply hits the stage to deliver an energy driven show using guitars, drums, and their voices. Nothing more, nothing less. This approach to their live performances has led to them sharing the stage with acts such as Highly Suspect, Papa Roach, Black Stone Cherry, Pop Evil, and more. 
Check out the Small Town Titans here!

title: LFS Feminist Consciousness-Raising Film Afternoons
description:
Lancaster Freethought Society
**Feminist Film Afternoons #2: Salt of the Earth (1954)**
**What happens when women discover that fighting for their families isn't enough—they must fight for their own equality, too?**
Join us for the second of five Feminist Consciousness-Raising Film Afternoons, featuring *Salt of the Earth*, a groundbreaking American film based on a real miners' strike in New Mexico.
When Mexican-American miners strike against dangerous working conditions and discriminatory wages, a court injunction prevents the men from picketing. Their wives step forward to take their places, while the men must assume responsibility for the households and children.
What begins as support for their husbands becomes something much more powerful: women discovering their own political agency.

**After the film, we'll discuss:**

* How did the women's understanding of their own oppression change through collective action?
* What happened when men and women exchanged their traditional responsibilities?
* Can a movement for equality succeed if women remain subordinate within that movement?

This is a relaxed, friendly afternoon of film and conversation—not a lecture or debate. Everyone is welcome to share their experiences and perspectives.

**The Details**

* **When:** Sunday, November 29, 2–5 PM
* **Where:** Private home in Millersville. Address provided individually to confirmed attendees.
* **Seating:** Limited to six guests.
* **Attendance:** Women have priority through Saturday. If spaces remain, men may RSVP beginning Saturday, November 28 at noon.
* **Guests:** No additional guests, please.

Each film afternoon stands on its own. Come to one or several—no preparation or ongoing commitment required.
**Bring your curiosity, your ideas, and your willingness to imagine something better!**

title: A Century of Winnie-the-Pooh
location: Lancaster, LPL Community Room
description:
Community, Presentation, Everyone

Winnie-the-Pooh is celebrating its 100th birthday this year! The stories A.A. Milne created have become classics that are as beloved now as they were when they were first published in October 1926. In celebration of the centennial of Milne’s timeless tales, join Dr. Sarah Jackson, Assistant Professor from the Department of Early, Middle, and Elementary Education at Millersville University to learn about how these beloved children’s stories have endured as they have been translated and adapted countless times since their publication 100 years ago. Dr. Jackson will focus on the influence of colonialism in the stories and consider how the animal characters try on—and resist—colonial language. All ages welcome, but this will be a lecture-style program geared toward the young at heart 😉Registration is helpful, but walk-ins will not be turned away.

title: Being One Online Spiritual Support Group
description:
Being One Center in Lancaster County
Life can be frustrating and distressing!
Sometimes we just feel overwhelmed, insecure, or lost!

The good news is, you're not alone!

We warmly invite you to check-in and connect with community in our Online Spiritual Support Group. In each meeting, we will discuss our current stressors and see how we can positively cope using our spiritual tools to overcome these challenges.

Together we can help each other grow and expand our consciousness for these high vibrational times.

Donations Greatly Appreciated!

This Event is lovingly hosted By Anna Bojczuk. Anna is a Registered nurse with over 40 years of experience as well as a gifted Energy worker. Anna is also long-time volunteer and inspiration in the Being One Center Community.

title: Monthly Club Meeting - "Wearables for Wildlife: Behind the Scenes with the Evolution of Wildlife Telemetry Technologies"
location: North Museum of Nature and Science, 400 College Ave, Lancaster, PA, 17603, United States
description:
Club Meeting – North Museum of Nature and Science, 400 College Ave, Lancaster, PA 17603 
Presented by Club President Andy McGann 
Andy McGann grew up birding in Southcentral Pennsylvania and his early experiences ultimately led to a career in the field of Movement Ecology. His time in academia, non-profits, consulting, and ultimately to a wildlife telemetry tech company spanned a timeframe that saw the science advance from analog radio telemetry to “smart devices” with GPS, accelerometers, and global Internet connectivity. In his career, Andy combined his experiences in ornithology with his love of technology and appreciation for geography in order to help wildlife researchers and organizations around the world obtain the scientific information needed to help conserve some of the rarest birds we have left. Andy will discuss the evolution of the technology, the current state-of-the-art, and paint a picture of where we are going.

title: Geminids Meteor Shower at Millport Conservancy
location: Millport Conservancy, 737 E. Millport Rd., Lititz, PA, 17543, United States
description:
[vc_row][vc_column width=”1/1″][vc_column_text uncode_shortcode_id=”128240″] 
Geminids are the most active meteor shower of the year!
Join us at Millport Conservancy on the night of Sunday, December 13th, to observe what could be the most spectacular meteor shower of the year! Far from the city lights of Lancaster, the darker skies of Millport mean we could see up to 30+ meteors, if the weather cooperates! 
The Geminids are the most active meteor shower of the year, and are considered one of the two best showers for viewing (along with August’s Perseids). The Geminids are unlike most other meteor showers, in that they are not likely caused by a debris field from a comet. Instead, the Geminids have been identified as being spawned from the debris field of 3200 Phaethon, which is what seems to be an asteroid. Astronomers believe Phaethon is an asteroid because it lacks the trail of a typical comet when it passes the Sun, and its spectra looks like that of a rocky asteroid. Additionally, the debris left behind by Phaethon is denser than that of a typical comet. 
However, the object does have a highly elliptical, or non-circular/”stretched out”, orbit, which is atypical for an asteroid but common for comets. Phaethon’s strange orbit gives astronomers pause when labeling it as “just” an asteroid, and some astronomers have proposed that Phaethon may actually be a “dead comet”, or even possibly an entirely new type of object that some astronomers are starting to call a “rock comet”. 
Whatever Phaethon is, the debris field it has left has made for great views here on Earth! Every year, around December 13th and 14th, the Earth passes through the debris field. When this happens, the Earth can be thought of as pushing through the debris, made up of tiny rocks, and pulling them into our atmosphere with the help of gravity. All the rocks burning up in our atmosphere is what can be seen as the meteor shower we all know and love. 
Keep an eye out in the coming weeks for more information about the North Museum’s Geminids Star Party, as well as general observing tips and information about the meteor shower![/vc_column_text][/vc_column][/vc_row]

Sometimes we just feel overwhelmed, insecure, or lost!

The good news is, you're not alone!

Together we can help each other grow and expand our consciousness for these high vibrational times.

Donations Greatly Appreciated!

This Event is lovingly hosted By Anna Bojczuk. Anna is a Registered nurse with over 40 years of experience as well as a gifted Energy worker. Anna is also long-time volunteer and inspiration in the Being One Center Community.

**Where:** [The Candy Factory](https://share.google/nqC7VtCS6IcDeBRyg)
**Cost:** Free & Open to the Public
**Ages:** All Ages

**Upcoming Dates**
July 11, July 25, Aug 8, Aug 22, Sept 5, Sept 19, Oct 3, Oct 17, Oct 31, Nov 14, Nov 28, Dec 9, Dec 23

*Do you have creative aspirations but never seem to make the time? Do you want the companionship of others to overcome your creative blocks and “just do it”?*

Creative Release provides spaces and resources that make artmaking accessible. Whether you’re an experienced artist or just looking to explore your creative side, Creative Release is a safe place to explore your ideas with others. Bring your ongoing projects or use the art materials available.

Don't have a project at the moment? That's just fine. I’ll have materials to share.
**What to Expect:**

* A welcoming, inclusive environment
* A variety of art materials to experiment with
* Demonstrations on how to use different art materials
* The opportunity to work on your personal projects
* The chance to meet and collaborate with fellow creatives
* A moment to relax, create, and escape the usual routine

**Who Should Join?**
Anyone and everyone! Bring an idea for a card, a knitting pattern you’ve been wanting to try, a shirt that needs mending, or a full-on canvas and paints. Most of all, bring your lovely self! We believe in the power of community and creativity.

[Event Link](https://www.jodavis.art/community-events-1/creative-release)

Whether you're into sweet contemporary rom-coms, high-heat historical reads, or paranormal romance, there's a seat for you at our table! description:
The Creative House of Lancaster
#### ***A Place to Make Art Together***

**When:** Every Other Saturday from 10am - 12pm
**Where:** [The Candy Factory](https://share.google/nqC7VtCS6IcDeBRyg)
**Cost:** Free & Open to the Public
**Ages:** All Ages

**Upcoming Dates**
July 11, July 25, Aug 8, Aug 22, Sept 5, Sept 19, Oct 3, Oct 17, Oct 31, Nov 14, Nov 28, Dec 9, Dec 23

*Do you have creative aspirations but never seem to make the time? Do you want the companionship of others to overcome your creative blocks and “just do it”?*

Creative Release provides spaces and resources that make artmaking accessible. Whether you’re an experienced artist or just looking to explore your creative side, Creative Release is a safe place to explore your ideas with others. Bring your ongoing projects or use the art materials available.

Don't have a project at the moment? That's just fine. I’ll have materials to share.

* A welcoming, inclusive environment
* A variety of art materials to experiment with
* Demonstrations on how to use different art materials
* The opportunity to work on your personal projects
* The chance to meet and collaborate with fellow creatives
* A moment to relax, create, and escape the usual routine

**Who Should Join?**
Anyone and everyone! Bring an idea for a card, a knitting pattern you’ve been wanting to try, a shirt that needs mending, or a full-on canvas and paints. Most of all, bring your lovely self! We believe in the power of community and creativity.

title: Creative Release Open Studio Saturday
description:
The Creative House of Lancaster
#### ***A Place to Make Art Together***

**When:** Every Other Saturday from 10am - 12pm
**Where:** [The Candy Factory](https://share.google/nqC7VtCS6IcDeBRyg)
**Cost:** Free & Open to the Public
**Ages:** All Ages

**Upcoming Dates**
July 11, July 25, Aug 8, Aug 22, Sept 5, Sept 19, Oct 3, Oct 17, Oct 31, Nov 14, Nov 28, Dec 9, Dec 23

*Do you have creative aspirations but never seem to make the time? Do you want the companionship of others to overcome your creative blocks and “just do it”?*

Creative Release provides spaces and resources that make artmaking accessible. Whether you’re an experienced artist or just looking to explore your creative side, Creative Release is a safe place to explore your ideas with others. Bring your ongoing projects or use the art materials available.

Don't have a project at the moment? That's just fine. I’ll have materials to share.
**What to Expect:**

* A welcoming, inclusive environment
* A variety of art materials to experiment with
* Demonstrations on how to use different art materials
* The opportunity to work on your personal projects
* The chance to meet and collaborate with fellow creatives
* A moment to relax, create, and escape the usual routine

**Who Should Join?**
Anyone and everyone! Bring an idea for a card, a knitting pattern you’ve been wanting to try, a shirt that needs mending, or a full-on canvas and paints. Most of all, bring your lovely self! We believe in the power of community and creativity.

title: Creative Release Open Studio Saturday
description:
The Creative House of Lancaster
#### ***A Place to Make Art Together***

**When:** Every Other Saturday from 10am - 12pm
**Where:** [The Candy Factory](https://share.google/nqC7VtCS6IcDeBRyg)
**Cost:** Free & Open to the Public
**Ages:** All Ages

**Upcoming Dates**
July 11, July 25, Aug 8, Aug 22, Sept 5, Sept 19, Oct 3, Oct 17, Oct 31, Nov 14, Nov 28, Dec 9, Dec 23

*Do you have creative aspirations but never seem to make the time? Do you want the companionship of others to overcome your creative blocks and “just do it”?*

Creative Release provides spaces and resources that make artmaking accessible. Whether you’re an experienced artist or just looking to explore your creative side, Creative Release is a safe place to explore your ideas with others. Bring your ongoing projects or use the art materials available.

Don't have a project at the moment? That's just fine. I’ll have materials to share.
**What to Expect:**

* A welcoming, inclusive environment
* A variety of art materials to experiment with
* Demonstrations on how to use different art materials
* The opportunity to work on your personal projects
* The chance to meet and collaborate with fellow creatives
* A moment to relax, create, and escape the usual routine

**Who Should Join?**
Anyone and everyone! Bring an idea for a card, a knitting pattern you’ve been wanting to try, a shirt that needs mending, or a full-on canvas and paints. Most of all, bring your lovely self! We believe in the power of community and creativity.

[Event Link](https://www.jodavis.art/community-events-1/creative-release)

title: Lancaster Scrapbooking & Papercrafting Monthly gathering
description:
Lancaster Scrapbooking, Cards & Papercrafts
Scrapbook, make cards, practice quilling, or paint!
Meeting on the third Tuesday, 6-10 p.m., at the Cozy Crop House. (Also meeting the next night, Wednesday, same time & place. You can come to one or both, and can leave your gear overnight.) A chance to meet & gather monthly with local scrapbookers & crafters, in an ideal crafting environment! Plenty of room to do your own thing while we socialize. Bring your own supplies & projects, or just sit back and relax with scrapping friends, and watch & learn a new technique.
Specific crafting events (eg. card classes, paint nights, etc) may be featured here as scheduled.
Bring snacks to share if you wish.
Meetup groups are charged a monthly administration fee which is currently paid in this group by a few members. VOLUNTARY donations of $1 or $2 into a group "kitty" will help us continue the group's open membership and online advertising. The rate it costs our _whole group_ is about $12/month for a 6-month commitment. Please do not feel you cannot come if you don't contribute--the fee is paid, and donations are voluntary to cover future fees.

description:
Night Shift 2026-27  
Overview: Experience the Lancaster Science Factory in a whole new way when you stay overnight! Explore over 75 hands-on exhibits, enjoy a pre-lights-out snack, unroll your sleeping bag in the exhibit hall, and have a light breakfast before you leave in the morning. Tickets: Tickets for the Night Shift are just $65 and include activity guides, a hands-on STEM workshop, snacks, and breakfast. This program is limited to children ages 6-12 and one adult (18+) is required for every three children. No adults will be admitted without children.
